panels.title: Edge HPA replicas (current / desired / min / max)
Edge HPA memory utilization vs target (%)
panels.description: REQUEST TIER ONLY, and the pod exclusion is load-bearing. This is a sum/sum ratio, which is only the HPA's own number while every pod in it has the SAME memory request. Deployment channels and edgeFunctions.workerTier all name their container `functions` too, and the HPA measures none of them, so an unscoped container= selector folds in pods that are not in the ratio and returns a figure that is nobody's. The worker tier happens to request the same 1.5Gi as the request tier at chart defaults (an earlier draft of this description said 1Gi, which was a superseded value), so equal requests are NOT the reason the filter can be dropped: the prod overlays put the request tier at 1.8Gi, and even at identical requests the HPA still does not measure worker or channel pods. The `edge_tier` label the chart adds is on the deno_* series from the ServiceMonitor, not on cAdvisor/kube-state-metrics, so the pod name is the discriminator available here. Selected POSITIVELY rather than by excluding the worker tier, which is the 2026-09-02 fix: `pod!~".*-functions-workers-.*"` still folded in every DEPLOYMENT CHANNEL pod (`<release>-functions-canary-...`), and the HPA does not measure those either -- so canary memory moved a panel whose whole job is to reproduce the HPA's own number. A request-tier pod is `<release>-functions-<rs-hash>-<suffix>`: exactly two dash-free segments after `-functions-`. The worker tier (`-functions-workers-<hash>-<suffix>`) and every channel (`-functions-<channel>-<hash>-<suffix>`) have three, so `pod=~".*-functions-[^-]+-[^-]+"` admits the request tier and nothing else -- and unlike an exclusion list it does not need editing when a channel is added. Prometheus anchors regex matchers implicitly, which is what makes the trailing segment count binding.

panels.title: Per-pod edge memory (MiB) — should plateau, not ramp
panels.description: Per-pod series cover BOTH edge tiers (they are per-pod, so mixing is fine and the worker tier is worth watching here). The ceiling is drawn per tier because the two limits differ: 4Gi on the request tier, 3584Mi on edgeFunctions.workerTier. A single max() across container="functions" would draw one 4Gi line and plot worker pods against a ceiling 512Mi higher than the one that will actually OOM-kill them. Both ceilings count POD NAME SEGMENTS rather than pattern-matching a tier name, which is the 2026-09-02 fix and makes the two operands consistent: `.*-functions-workers-.*` also captured a deployment channel named `workers-blue` (`<release>-functions-workers-blue-<hash>-<suffix>`), and channels inherit the REQUEST tier's 4Gi limit, so max() would have drawn 4Gi as the worker ceiling and hidden worker pods approaching their real 3584Mi cap -- the one failure this panel exists to make visible. A worker-tier pod has exactly two dash-free segments after `-functions-workers-`; a `workers-<something>` channel has three. A channel named exactly `workers` would be genuinely indistinguishable here, which is why the chart refuses it outright (edge-functions-worker-tier.yaml), so the segment count is sufficient rather than merely likely.
